# HAWKING ULTRAGOAL
## Deep ModelLake passes → deterministic Gravity → internal Star NR deployment → DARKMATTER/Accelerator → optional NX

**Planning revision: 2026-09-15**  
**Purpose:** A resumable implementation/research mission for the existing Hawking Goal system.  
**Evidence boundary:** This brief records the user's latest intended scope and recommended operating gates. It does not attest live credentials, available credit, a running Goal, deployed code, model qualification, hardware support, or new performance. Suggested budgets require actual authorization. This is a mission brief, not a fourth constitution or a replacement scheduler.

> Build Hawking into a system that can deeply understand admitted source models, construct and independently qualify cheaper native representations, reuse the discovered methods without routine LLM supervision, deploy a useful local Star Family, and improve its real physical execution. Preserve the option to compile directly from a source package to an immutable NX without requiring a user-visible intermediate NR file.

## 1. Apply the latest scope, not the earlier shallow-screening steer

The user has clarified that the first population pass is **not** merely model-card screening. Every specimen in the frozen, authorized ModelLake cohort receives substantive anatomical, behavioral, state, representation, and native-execution work. The campaign attempts to achieve **at most 1.0 COMPLETE EBPW and at least 100 accepted generated tokens/second** for each language-generation specimen, while retaining its declared capability and continuation-state contract.

The second population pass concentrates additional engineering on the selected Star Family and turns reusable discoveries into executable Gravity procedures. It is not just another popularity ranking.

This supersedes the earlier instruction that most lake models should receive only shallow screening. It does not authorize unbounded spending or unrestricted model acquisition. Inexpensive feasibility checks are still useful to order the work; they must not replace the assigned deep obligation or be counted as a completed collapse.

Use **Pass A: population discovery and collapse** and **Pass B: Star engineering and method transfer** for these two sweeps. Preserve the existing constitutional Odyssey obligations—Discover, Develop/Transfer, Attack/Falsify—inside them. Do not silently delete the falsification obligation, invent new eras, or create competing terminology in runtime schemas.

Read the latest `HAWKING.md`, `H-ROADMAP.md`, `H-DARKMATTER.md`, current Goal/WorkUnit owners, ModelLake scheduling authority, artifact registry, and relevant receipts. Use current source/runtime facts over old assistant summaries. Read task-relevant sections rather than reinjecting entire documents every turn.

## 2. Establish the real starting state

Before mutation, identify:

- the actual current source tree, dirty changes, active worktrees, loaded binaries, and protected experiments;
- the current native execution, remote-provider, tool, budget, checkpoint, and verifier owners;
- the exact installed hardware, available storage, memory headroom, and existing platform approvals;
- the current ModelLake source-revision inventory and any acquisition, retention, or reference holds;
- the real available OpenRouter credential and funded allowance, without exposing either secret values or unrelated account data.

The last supplied report said the current Hawking implementation was in the dirty main checkout and that a separate remote-cognition worktree contained an older HCLI-era branch. **Verify this before selecting an implementation base.** Do not mistake an isolated but obsolete checkout for current code. Where isolation is required, use a coordinator-approved snapshot of the relevant current changes, with attributable base/diff identities and no loss of unrelated work.

A key exported in an unrelated Terminal does not establish that this worker or daemon can read it. Validate the current Hawking secret resolver in the process that will actually call the provider. Do not read a key into the model's context, print it, include it in process diagnostics, or weaken Keychain access controls to avoid an approval prompt.

No publication, remote push, repository-visibility change, purchase, firmware change, or unrelated system alteration follows from this mission.

## 3. Maintain one owner and protect Flash

The main Codex lane exclusively owns current Flash-Next/Pulsar scientific and performance work. Remote workers may consume immutable, published-to-the-campaign Flash evidence; they must not change its kernels, route observations, candidate binaries, acceptance contract, NR accounting, active worktree, or protected resource leases.

Represent ownership through the existing authoritative mechanism, with stale-owner recovery and attributable handoff. An `active_owner` string alone is not concurrency control. Many read-only analyses can coexist; there is one authorized mutation writer for each protected object.

Hawking owns Goals, tools, state, mutation, verification, cost, and scheduling. OpenRouter supplies replaceable cognition. Do not revive HCLI, AgentOS, HIDE, Grok Bot, or a second model server as an active owner. Do not create a new cloud-agent orchestration framework.

Separate Git isolation from physical-resource isolation. CPU builds, disk scans, memory allocation, and non-Flash GPU probes can still contaminate Flash timing. Heavy local work needs an approved resource window. Remote source analysis can proceed while the local experimental device is reserved.

The user has not authorized a C/C++ rewrite through this mission. Keep the current Rust/native direction and qualified device-language implementations. Migrate code only where a measured recurring cost, ownership defect, or necessary interface justifies it.

## 4. Qualify the remote workforce before a long mission

Use the single existing remote-provider implementation for generic `/v1` requests and Hawking WorkUnits. Do not rebuild the gateway unless live evidence reveals a blocking defect.

Verify the installed path, live catalog, exact model identity, non-streaming and streaming calls, usage accounting, scoped tool round trips, local access policy, and a small read-only WorkUnit. Generic clients' tool calls return to those clients; they do not gain access to Hawking-private tools.

Before unattended write work, qualify a disposable staged-edit task and a controlled checkpoint/restart test. Test restart only on this mission's owned worker or an isolated test instance; never kill a shared daemon carrying Flash or unrelated work. Preserve tool-call IDs, completed-operation identities, pending transactions, and budget reservations. Unknown completion is not permission to execute a side effect twice.

A cancellation test must distinguish closing a local connection from confirmed upstream cancellation. Unknown final provider cost remains unknown or conservatively reserved until reconciled.

Verify each model's actual supported parameters. Do not make provider-enforced JSON Schema an unnecessary universal entrance requirement: a tool-capable model may return structured tool arguments that Hawking validates locally. Unsupported features must remain explicit. Never silently strip a safety-critical requested parameter to make the request succeed.

Reasoning-token usage belongs in cost accounting. Human-visible logs and receipts should not contain raw reasoning traces. Preserve protocol-required opaque continuation data only through an explicitly approved private provider-session mechanism; do not destroy required round-trip fields under the mistaken assumption that redacting the user display and erasing protocol state are the same operation. If current privacy policy cannot support the provider's required protocol, select a compatible route or report the specific incompatibility.

## 5. Starting model policy and pilot

**Starting lead candidate:** `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`.  
**Low-cost comparison worker:** `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, paid route.  
**Sparse difficult-review candidate:** `moonshotai/kimi-k3` only with a separately allowed cost envelope.

These are recommendations, not permission to assume superiority or spend. Refresh the exact catalog and eligible endpoint capabilities/prices before activation. Do not use an unversioned “latest” alias as reproducibility evidence. Bind request, served model, provider, settings, and any provider-exposed revision; when weight-level identity is unavailable, say so.

Run the same small real Hawking task set against DeepSeek and GLM: one source/state interpretation question, one small tested implementation, and one critique of deliberately flawed evidence. Use equivalent scoped tools, starting source, tests, and output requirements. Evaluate accepted work, invalid tool calls, repaired defects, context growth, total cost, wall time, and verifier overturns. Start with a maximum US$5 combined pilot **only if that amount is actually authorized**. Keep a smaller configured ceiling if one already applies.

Use the better demonstrated worker as lead. Retain the other for a genuinely independent bounded review when valuable. Do not spawn a recursive agent tree or make a paid reviewer certify its own work. Model disagreement is evidence to investigate, not a voting system for truth.

## 6. Spending and resource authority

Maintain separate ledgers for OpenRouter credits, Codex/subscription allowance, external compute rental, and local hardware time/energy/storage. A previous mention of “$20 remaining” does not establish which account it belongs to. A credit balance is not a spending mandate.

Suggested rollout, subject to approval:

1. Up to US$5 for live qualification and comparative pilot.
2. A total US$20 initial campaign tranche, including the pilot, with an operator reserve.
3. Further US$25–50 tranches only after useful accepted artifacts and an updated forecast justify them.

The discussion's US$100–300 broader research envelope is a planning reserve, not automatically authorized money or a completion price.

Before each request, reserve the conservative cost of its allowed input/output/reasoning and known billable tools. Reservations must be atomic across concurrent workers and survive restart. Include retries, abandoned streams, review calls, and failed attempts in accounting. Missing usage is not zero cost. Stop new paid admission when available authorized credit is insufficient.

Use bounded steps and explicit next-result events. Do not spend model turns polling a compiler or a GPU that can report completion mechanically. Do not equate slow progress with cheap progress; show incurred dollars and valid information gained.

Begin with one remote lead and at most one independent remote helper. Limit local heavy execution through the canonical resource owner, not remote API concurrency.

## 7. Freeze the cohort and comparison contracts

Create a versioned cohort from the existing lake inventory, with exact source revisions and ownership. The latest user intent covers the current lake, not an indefinitely expanding stream of future downloads. Reconcile an older fifteen-specimen cap through the canonical scheduling owner and record any authorized expansion explicitly. No automatic additions merely because an API catalog contains another model.

For each specimen, preserve source format, parameter-count definition, tokenizer/configuration, architecture, modality, state, missing shards, licenses, source/reference access, local feasibility, current controls, and the cheapest informative next experiment.

Do not treat a hosted endpoint sharing a model name as an exact oracle for local weights. Exact reproduction requires a suitably pinned local/reference implementation or another genuinely bound reference. Hosted behavioral tests can be useful but must carry their weaker identity/fidelity scope.

Declare the numerical and capability contract **before** optimizing. Distinguish bit-exact values, equivalent functions, matching selected trajectories, distributional fidelity, and empirical task performance. Do not promise “zero intelligence loss” from a finite benchmark.

For non-language specimens, record appropriate native performance measures rather than inventing token TPS. Do not label those specimens as satisfying the language 100-TPS gate.

## 8. Pass A — Deep discovery, collapse, and real native execution

Every admitted specimen gets substantive work, scaled to the actual novelty of its mechanisms. Reusing a verified applicable method is depth through accumulated knowledge, not superficial screening.

For each specimen:

1. Bind anatomy and execution/state semantics. Inspect normalization, projections, attention or recurrence, routing, expert topology, embeddings/head, positional state, modality paths, arithmetic materialization, and rare routes as relevant.
2. Recover an independent control at the required scope. Preserve immutable source observations and a stable reference. Build only the missing discriminators, not another full general framework.
3. Inventory required bytes and native execution costs. Separate source storage, candidate artifact, active bytes/token, state, scratch, and process footprint.
4. Apply applicable Gravity methods with controlled precision/representation changes. Novel structures can justify new kernels, methods, fitting, or explicitly traced Nova—not a silent change to source truth.
5. Build an actual complete candidate and execute its advertised scope natively. Do not indefinitely substitute layer demonstrations for full closure.
6. Validate held-out prompts, future state, long context, rare routes, tools, and relevant modalities. Include deliberately faulty controls to test the evaluator.
7. Measure free-running native performance using the declared workload. Keep teacher-forced, forced-route, selected-expert-union, cached-output, and short bounded-replay measurements separate.
8. Internalize a real reusable method, reference, failure rule, test, kernel, or exact remaining question.

The target is at most 1.0 COMPLETE EBPW and at least 100 accepted generated TPS. Record the programme's new 100-TPS floor separately from any stronger existing Flash contract; the remote lane must not rewrite the protected Flash gate. Higher performance/lower size remain objectives when supported by evidence.

An unresolved or budget-stopped specimen is not a successful collapse. Preserve the target, the strongest achieved result, exact blocker, next falsifier, and reopening condition. Failed searches do not prove impossibility; missing support does not become successful native execution.

## 9. Correctness must remain independent of candidate observations

Do not repeat the Flash-style one-row route refresh as a general search strategy. After repeated same-class divergence, change the diagnostic to gather the necessary evidence more efficiently under a frozen build and explicit resource bounds.

Distinguish three objects:

- independent source/reference truth;
- a current candidate's own observed execution;
- a benchmark fixture used to reproduce that candidate.

Changing a fixture to match a candidate can establish reproducibility. It does **not** establish fidelity to the source. A checksum or “sealed” filename does not create independent validation.

Same-set route reordering can still affect weighted finite-precision reduction. Preserve identity/weight association and validate downstream state/output under the declared policy. Membership changes need scientific interpretation; they are not automatically “only stale provenance.”

Where safe, collect a complete candidate route observation in a separate untimed discovery pass, provision required expert access within the approved envelope, then freeze and repeat. If a compact cache lacks newly selected experts, do not skip those experts or fabricate outputs to finish the census. Use a controlled observation-only loading path or report the precise access limitation.

The timed resident path must compute real routing and supported continuation behavior. It must not obtain apparent speed by knowing the future token chain or expert set from an answer transcript unless explicitly reported as a non-promotable microbenchmark.

## 10. Complete storage, fidelity, and throughput gates

Use a fixed source denominator:

`COMPLETE_EBPW = 8 × required model-specific runnable bytes / declared N_source`.

Count indices, codebooks, coefficients, generated constants, fragment libraries, routing tables, exceptions, tokenizer/configuration, native model-specific code, and any required fallback. Disclose shared-runtime accounting and absolute complete bundle bytes. Keep transient expansion, resident state, peak memory, staging, and fragmentation visible separately.

Do not change the denominator after deleting model components. A deliberately specialized descendant needs a traceable semantic scope and an evaluation showing what was retained and what changed.

The size gate and speed gate must be achieved by the **same exact candidate lineage/build/profile** under its declared fidelity contract. Do not combine one artifact's size with another artifact's TPS or a cloud provider's speed.

Measure full-model single-stream accepted decode after a stated warmup and prompt regime, with sufficient output length and repetitions, reported variance, and representative short/long contexts. Report prefill, TTFT, startup, tool latency, and aggregate concurrency separately. A high aggregate batched rate is not a high single-stream rate.

Use an independent workload/evaluator snapshot, unknown during candidate selection where appropriate. Do not “repair” evaluation results by teaching the candidate the test and then reusing that same test as held-out evidence.

If a current body is slow, first reconcile a full-token timeline and active-traffic ledger. Use critical-path attribution; do not sum overlapping CPU/GPU durations into false wall time. Profile experimentally before prescribing fusion, lower precision, or model surgery. Runtime-only failure does not itself prove a particular representation change will succeed.

## 11. Pass B — Star Family engineering and transfer

Select the user's intended persistent local roles from the measured descendants, not from model reputation alone. Recover the current candidate list and personal role choices from canonical project records. Do not invent weight availability or assign every desired upstream model to a role before qualification.

Possible roles include fast local engineering, deeper reasoning, independent checking, and a small low-overhead worker. The current canon uses Pulsar, Magnetar, and Themis; other user-selected names remain configuration, not new provider products.

For selected Stars:

- run a deeper joint search over representation, kernels, state, layout, scheduling, and physical fit;
- test transfer of population discoveries on unseen contexts and appropriate anchor models;
- apply Nova only with explicit training scope, data/teacher access, compute budget, lineage, rollback, and independent evaluation;
- compare capability and usable task goodput against the incumbent, not just decode speed;
- establish load/reuse/memory/context behavior and actual engineering competence;
- prove checkpoint/resume and tool use at the role's real authority level.

Do not require all Stars to stay co-resident. Installation on internal storage and simultaneous allocation into CPU/GPU memory are different milestones. Load roles as needed and measure any coexistence claim.

Keep cross-model learning bounded. A new discovery may justify revisiting a few anchors or selected Stars; it does not automatically restart every finished specimen.

## 12. Make Gravity dynamic but deterministic

The objective is not a giant hard-coded list of model names. Build reusable typed procedures with applicability predicates, inputs, precision/state assumptions, execution costs, independent checks, and failure/reopen conditions.

Separate three paths:

1. **Reuse:** exact admitted artifact/build or validated cache hit.
2. **Known-method construction:** deterministic selection, calibration, packing, compilation, and validation using implemented methods.
3. **Research:** an unfamiliar mechanism or failed gate invokes a separately budgeted investigation, possibly with model assistance.

The first two should work with remote cognition disabled. The third must not pretend it is already automated science.

Given fixed source, target profile, numerical policy, recipe/version, and seed where applicable, produce reproducible decisions/artifact identities at the contract's supported scope. Hardware timing varies; deterministic workflow does not imply identical performance samples or bit-identical outputs across arbitrary devices/compilers.

Validate reuse with positive and negative controls: compatible new inputs work, unsupported inputs are rejected or explicitly classified, stale compiler/device assumptions invalidate only relevant caches, and changed shared methods revalidate dependent artifacts.

Measure separately: inventory/selection latency, source I/O, calibration, fitting/search, compile, evaluation, deployment, warm reload, and source-to-qualified-artifact elapsed time. Report AI calls/tokens avoided by actual mechanical execution, not by estimated replacement of imagined conversations.

## 13. CLI and internal storage experience

Implement the requested interaction through the current `hawking` / optional `h` front door. These are desired interactions, not assertions that exact commands already exist.

`hawking select` should present clear groups, for example:

- **Ready:** admitted NR/NX artifacts, exact revisions, measured profile/role.
- **Sources / not yet collapsed:** available source specimens and truthful current status.
- **Candidates / blocked:** research artifacts with the precise missing gate.

After selection, present applicable actions: inspect, Gravity, optional Nova, optional NX compilation, serve, or web. A raw source can be selected for Gravity without falsely being advertised as an admitted native serving model. Headless clients need explicit equivalents and useful exit/status behavior, not forced interactive menus.

All surfaces share model identity and authority. Selecting a model in one client must not silently replace another client's active model or Goal.

Install qualified Star NR closures onto the chosen internal-storage destination after validating capacity, hashes, complete dependencies, permissions, and rollback. Preserve source/reference holds; do not delete the lake as a side effect of installation. Prove that serving no longer reaches back into an uncounted external source or development cache. Do not physically unplug a drive carrying another active experiment merely to test closure; use controlled access isolation.

## 14. Finish the usable platform, not an endless UI redesign

H Web is a Hawking surface, not a separate project. Complete the features necessary for ordinary conversation and a real Goal: selection, progress, interruption, steering, terminal result, checkpoint, later retrieval, and authenticated access.

A user-facing `/goal` may be a command parser for the existing durable Goal system. It is not an OpenRouter endpoint or proof that an API model persists independently.

Demonstrate a local Star accomplishing a meaningful bounded task with tools, test/repair, safe staging, independent review, interruption recovery, and a durable result. Prove the same Goal can use an admitted remote or local worker without changing its acceptance contract.

Reduce cloud dependence by demonstrated task class. Do not declare “OpenRouter no longer needed” solely because several models load. Maintain an explicit remote fallback/escalation policy with its budget, rather than deleting useful optional capability.

## 15. Start DARKMATTER as an integrated execution-and-observation programme

The main sustained DARKMATTER campaign follows the two model passes, method integration, and qualified local Star deployment under the user's requested ordering. Independent prerequisites can be prepared earlier only when they do not consume the protected critical path or contradict current authorization.

Do not create a circular dependency where every Star must attain its ultimate physical performance before any needed hardware integration may be examined. If a model target depends on an unavailable base device contract, record that dependency explicitly and request/execute only the already-authorized bounded prerequisite—not a disguised full new campaign.

Accelerator is the execution capability inside DARKMATTER, not a competing product or a project that must wait for all hardware mysteries to be solved.

Practical order:

1. Establish real CPU/Apple execution baselines and identify the actual external card/bridge/OS/firmware/compiler tuple.
2. Build or qualify the minimal base device path: allocation, transfers, submission, synchronization, completion, cancellation, and recoverable failure handling.
3. Establish an independently checked useful kernel and then a complete representative model/region workload.
4. Observe and optimize that real execution: arithmetic/compiler behavior, layout, occupancy where measurable, register/temporary pressure, launch gaps, cache/translation behavior, contention, and transfers.
5. Compare Apple-only, whole-external, partitioned, and useful concurrent plans on matched inputs.
6. Feed verified consequences into Gravity procedures, kernels, memory plans, and device profiles; retest the affected Stars.

Do not assume an external GPU adds its bandwidth to Apple UMA, creates coherent shared memory, or produces speedup automatically. A selected local-only plan is valid when transfers make a split worse. Test real full-request behavior.

Cloud workers can author and review before a local investigator is mature, within scope; they cannot replace actual device/reference access. Extended local self-directed physical investigation still needs demonstrated worker competence, independent checking, stable native controls, resource leases, and a recoverable host.

Do not make a new FPGA/custom-chip simulator a prerequisite. FPGA hardware and dedicated FPGA research are deferred. Retain normal deterministic tests, mocks, replay controls, and failure-injection tests: these are how reset/cancellation paths are checked safely even when real GPU hardware is present.

## 16. Optional NX: ordinary compilation and deeper functional engineering

Keep NR and NX distinct without forcing the user to manage both artifacts.

**NR:** mutable, inspectable tensor/program/hybrid semantics, learned information, lineage, and portable requirements.  
**NX:** immutable versioned executable closure for an exact semantic revision and target/fidelity contract. Runtime state remains dynamic. Recompilation produces a new NX identity.

First establish ordinary NX lowering where useful: specialize shapes/layouts, pack data, select kernels, plan buffers and schedules, compile, and verify the complete deployment. Ordinary NX may preserve the same represented computation and may deliver no additional compression; measure its value.

Then pursue deeper functional compilation under an explicit research envelope: jointly smaller interfaces and future-relevant state; shared executable fragments; small arithmetic/lookup functions; learned constants; residual correction; and, when justified, Nova for compileability. Compare against both ordinary graph optimization and the best direct representation.

LUTs are candidate local computational primitives, not a database of every possible prompt/answer. Count their encoders, wiring, tables, state, dispatch, combination, and exceptions. GPU arithmetic/bitwise code may be the better realization; future FPGA LUT mapping is optional and separately qualified.

A region-level result is not whole-model fidelity. Require held-out trajectories, rare routes, delayed-state counterexamples, complete dependencies, actual native speed, and retained task capability before a full standalone claim.

## 17. Direct safetensors-to-NX workflow

Support this as an eventual single user operation through the **same** Gravity pipeline:

`source package → validated semantic import → intermediate NR/IR → optional transformations → target lowering → independent checks → immutable NX closure`.

The user need not explicitly save or install an intermediate `.nr`. Retain the semantic identity, reproducible recipe, and enough internal intermediate/checkpoint information to establish provenance and support recovery. Do not bypass source semantics, reference checks, or complete accounting.

A safetensors file stores tensors; source import also needs the relevant architecture/configuration, tokenizer, state definitions, and permitted implementation metadata. Do not execute arbitrary model repository code as a consequence of opening a tensor file.

Offer the equivalent of “retain editable NR” when the user plans to use Nova. If only NX was retained, modification may require reconstructing the exact semantic intermediate or returning to the source. Do not promise that a lossy/compiled NX can always be inverted into its former mutable NR.

Use semantic checkpoints internally even in a direct workflow. Deliberate learned/function changes remain a derived NR or explicit semantic delta; a one-command UI does not exempt lineage.

Direct compilation does not itself establish extreme compression. A 1–10 GB descendant of a terabyte-scale ancestor is a separate measured research outcome, not a promise of the file format or an “abstraction squared” multiplier.

## 18. Model fit and construction resources

Keep these questions separate:

- Does the source exist on disk?
- Can an independent source oracle execute at the needed scope?
- Can the candidate be constructed within current resources?
- Does the complete deployment fit on internal storage?
- Does its working set fit the chosen memory domains?
- Can it sustain the required accepted throughput?

At 1 EBPW, one trillion source parameters correspond to 125 GB of model-specific bytes; a 2.8-trillion-parameter source corresponds to 350 GB. Runtime state/scratch/headroom are additional. A common 1-EBPW target does not make every giant source locally resident.

Streaming, out-of-core construction, layer-local experiments, smaller calibration corpora, and compact references can help specific stages. None automatically establishes cheap full-source teaching, whole-model independence, or fast inference. Forecast these costs separately from remote model API cost.

Do not assume the incoming GPU or an unpurchased FPGA removes the construction bottleneck. Hardware arrival is a new measurable capability, not an accepted speed multiplier.

## 19. Durable progress and anti-loop rules

One UltraGoal may own the programme; it must compile to bounded durable WorkUnits, not one enormous indefinitely growing chat.

At each expensive step preserve input/build identities, hypothesis, reference, allowed mutations, resource window, expected discriminator, incurred cost, output, independent check, next action, and stop conditions.

Repeated unchanged failures trigger a different discriminator, a bounded implementation repair, or explicit scoped escalation. Renaming the same failed output or updating an expected answer is not scientific progress. Avoid repeated source loading/rebuilding when unchanged dependencies permit safe reuse.

No-progress detection should use useful changes in artifacts, uncertainty, executable methods, validated results, or closed obligations. A long transcript, high token count, zero exit status, or `CONTINUE` marker does not meet it.

Use existing terminal states. Distinguish target hit, unresolved research, missing access, resource block, and budget exhaustion. If every model is required to achieve the target, do not call the entire pass complete while models remain below it. A well-documented negative may complete an assigned question without satisfying the model's performance target.

## 20. Acceptance and reporting

Keep separate milestone reports for:

1. Live remote transport/tool/WorkUnit qualification.
2. Frozen population and deep Pass A work.
3. Per-model complete artifact, state/fidelity, and performance targets.
4. Executable cross-model method transfer.
5. Selected Star Pass B improvements and role competence.
6. Internal-storage artifact closure and operator usability.
7. Base external-device qualification.
8. Integrated DARKMATTER improvements on real workloads.
9. Ordinary NX and, separately, deeper functional NX.
10. Direct source-to-NX workflow with complete provenance.

Each checkpoint reports what changed, what was actually executed, artifact/build identity, exact scope of correctness, bytes, working memory, accepted throughput, total remote tokens/cost, local device time, tests, unresolved questions, budget remaining, ownership, and the next cheapest informative experiment.

Do not add test counts from unrelated builds into a synthetic assurance total. Do not automatically label old failures pre-existing; show the matched base result when attribution matters. Do not accept a modified verifier as independent evidence unless that verifier change was separately reviewed and qualified.

Publish no public announcement, release, external repository push, model redistribution, or benchmark marketing as part of this mission. Preserve the user's later choice between private use, delayed disclosure, and public release.

## 21. Immediate execution order

Continue from the actual current frontier. First repair only remaining live-provider/worker blockers, qualify the small worker comparison within existing spending authority, freeze the lake cohort and ownership map, and start one high-information **non-Flash** deep specimen pass using the current methods.

Before admitting a second unfamiliar architecture, report the first specimen's real method-transfer burden, source/reference access, local device time, total API cost, strongest achieved artifact, target gap, and next intervention. Use that evidence to update the population schedule.

Keep the full programme in durable state. Do not demand a new “continue” prompt for already-authorized, affordable, safe transitions. Do stop for genuinely new financial/access/publication/destructive authority. A document cannot keep a dead process running; record real Goal/worker identity and report stopped or detached state truthfully.

## A. Current external-worker price snapshot

The model pages checked for this brief list the following per-million-token USD rates. Lowest listed prices can be promotional or endpoint-specific; privacy/capability constraints may select another rate.

| Model ID | Input | Output | Qualification note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | $0.15 | $0.60 | Starting lead candidate. Page lists tool calling, but not provider-enforced `response_format`; validate structured results in Hawking. |

Example **metered inference costs**, excluding credit-purchase fees, paid tools, additional retries, and compute rental:

| 2M input + 0.4M output | $0.54 | $0.25 | $7.95 |
| 40M input + 8M output | $10.80 | $5.00 | $159.00 |
| 200M input + 40M output | $54.00 | $25.00 | $795.00 |

“Output” here must include all billed reasoning/output tokens, not just visible final text. These are calculations for stipulated token volumes, **not estimates that either Odyssey will consume those volumes or finish for those prices**.

OpenRouter's FAQ lists a 5.5% credit-purchase fee with a $0.80 minimum. Account checkout is authoritative for the actual charge. Cash paid, usable credits, incurred inference cost, and approved mission budget are distinct.

## B. Project-time planning model

No completed current full-body source-faithful low-EBPW/100-TPS Flash endpoint is established by the supplied record. Do not infer that the remaining lake already has an implemented universal sub-1-EBPW path.

For planning only, an illustrative fifteen-source/four-Star scenario might allocate 0.5–2 productive days per mostly supported first-pass specimen, 2–5 days per selected Star in Pass B, and 5–10 days for shared integration/qualification. The arithmetic is about 20.5–60 productive days, or roughly 4–12 five-day working weeks. These assumptions require unusually good method transfer and source access; they are not measured Hawking productivity.

Several unfamiliar state/architecture mechanisms, expensive teacher access, fitting campaigns, or new backend work can extend this to months or longer. Successful universal attainment of every research target has no justified completion date from present evidence. Re-estimate after the pilot and after each independent architecture family.

API speed does not set local GPU availability, source I/O, compile time, test duration, or successful research iteration count. Parallel remote workers do not multiply the number of uncontended local GPU lanes.

## C. Source basis and scope

Project basis: current conversation's explicit revisions; `HAWKING.md` §§12–21 and 30; `H-ROADMAP(20260915-000652).md` §§7–17; `H-DARKMATTER.md` §§1–3 and physical programme. The two deep sweeps, current-lake scope, 1.0/100 programme targets, source/ready selector separation, internal-storage intent, and deferred FPGA campaign are latest-user directions, not claims that older documents already contained them.
